chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,
The Bedouins say: We believe. Say: You do not believe but say, We are Muslims; and Emān (belief) has not yet entered into your hearts
So he said to me: Do you not see that the Emān (faith) is other than Al-Islām?
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Islam and Emāa according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the theological distinction between Islam (external submission) and Iman (internal conviction) by referencing the Quranic critique of the Bedouins in Surah Al-Hujurat. This hadith establishes that while Islam may be declared verbally, true Iman is a deeper spiritual state that must penetrate the heart, a nuance central to Shia usul al-din. The Imam’s rhetorical question emphasizes that the two terms are not synonymous, highlighting the progression from outward compliance to inward certainty.
